role: Negative tests and security-boundary regression coverage versus production behavior

scope.application_commit_reviewed: e625ee7 with concurrent working-tree network/runtime fixes
additional_read: Previously completed complete DirectDownloader.kt and MediaEngine.kt reads connecting the tested boundaries to request/format construction
docs/SECURITY.md references discovered; no external source or platform guarantee inferred
scope.method: Read-only static comparison of negative-test assertions, fixtures and production call paths. No source/test/build edits, builds, test execution, device interaction or publication.

verified_observations: LiteralNetworkBoundaryTest exercises the production secureClient with literal-host validation and counts DNS/socket attempts. Both counters must remain zero, so a generic transport exception alone cannot falsely satisfy the test. A separate test passes a redirect through DirectDownloader.request and asserts only one request reached the test transport.

The older DirectDownloaderTest.rejectionsPrivateRedirectTargetThroughProductionDns-style test checks only an initial blocked loopback URL, despite its redirect-oriented name. Current LiteralNetworkBoundaryTest supplies the actual redirect boundary regression, so this naming weakness does not establish a masked production defect.

PublicProxyTest uses per-session credentials, rejects missing/wrong/other-session credentials and private/wrong-port targets, and records a resolved public InetSocketAddress before a second private DNS answer is rejected. Production PublicProxy validates the full answer list and connects that address rather than resolving the hostname again.

HeaderRepresentationTest exercises the actual HttpRepresentation helper against conflicting repeated Content-Encoding/Content-Length/Content-Type/Content-Range/ETag headers. Production direct and parallel transfer paths invoke the same helper before accepting body bytes.

DirectDownloaderTest seeds a real ResumeJournal and asserts invalid ranges or weak/changed validators leave the prior durable prefix unchanged. Its public-logical-URL-to-loopback transport is explicitly test-only and is not treated as production DNS coverage.

FormatSelectorTest rejects selector expressions/malformed pairs and compares allowlisted literal-ID construction. MediaEngine constructs structured wrapper options and applies the same selector helper.

ProxyTransportTest is explicitly opt-in and compares complete byte counts/hashes through Java and bundled Python CONNECT paths; static inspection does not promote a skipped optional network case into passed runtime evidence.
limitations: No test was executed; all observations concern test source and production wiring, not current passing status.
No broad penetration-test, certificate-endpoint compatibility, every-address-registry or arbitrary native-helper network coverage is claimed.
Security/test gaps alone were not filed as defects without a demonstrated material failed boundary or assertion that hides it.
Maximum-two finding cap yielded zero new proven actionable defects in the selected high-risk scope. Concurrent edits may change the final tree.
